title: Social Allostasis & Affect-Based Bonding in Artificial Agents
affiliation: University of Hertfordshire (PhD) → DICE Lab, University of Gothenburg → independent
description: My core, long-running research programme. It uses agent-based modelling and, more recently, active inference to treat social bonds and relationships as adaptive, allostatic-like regulatory mechanisms shared by biological and artificial social agents. It began with simulating oxytocin- and cortisol-like social buffering in simulated agent societies (my PhD thesis), and has since grown to cover physiological and biobehavioural proxies for bonding in human-robot interaction, a formal active-inference account of allostatic regulation under stress, and, most recently, an argument for treating trust and social bonding as genuinely separate constructs when evaluating human-robot relationships.

outputs.title: Modeling Affect-Based Relationships and Social Allostasis as Mechanisms for Adaptation in Social Groups
Modelling the Social Buffering Hypothesis in an Artificial Life Environment
The Long-Term Efficacy of “Social Buffering” in Artificial Social Agents: Contextual Affective Perception Matters
Surprise! Using Physiological Stress for Allostatic Regulation Under the Active Inference Framework
What Are We Measuring? Bonding, Trust, and the Evaluation of Human-Robot Relationships

audience: Students and academics interested in agent-based modelling, active inference, affective computing, or methods for evaluating human-robot relationships.

title: SARP-DCI: Socially Assistive Robot Partners for Digitized Cognitive Intervention Therapy
affiliation: EUTOPIA-SIF MSCA Fellowship, DICE Lab, University of Gothenburg
description: A fellowship project, and the wider collaborative programme it grew into, developing socially assistive robots and gamified digital adaptations of the Differential Outcomes Procedure (DOP) for cognitive intervention with people with neurocognitive disorders and related populations. Carried out with Robert Lowe's group at DICE Lab, it spans robot-mediated visuospatial memory training, affective-linguistic mutual learning between humans and robots, automatic detection of user engagement, and the DigiDOP framework itself.

outputs.title: Differential Outcomes Training of Visuospatial Memory: A Gamified Approach Using a Socially Assistive Robot
DigiDOP: A Framework for Applying Digital Technology to the Differential Outcomes Procedure (DOP) for Cognitive Interventions in Persons with Neurocognitive Disorders
Human-Robot Mutual Learning through Affective-Linguistic Interaction and Differential Outcomes Training
Deep Learning Approaches for User Engagement Detection in Human-Robot Interaction: A Scoping Review
Exploring Task and Social Engagement in Companion Social Robots: A Comparative Analysis of Feedback Types

audience: Students and academics working on assistive robotics, cognitive rehabilitation technology, or HRI for clinical and ageing populations.

title: Diversity Creates Diversity: Rewilding & Participatory Complex Systems Modelling
affiliation: NERC Discipline Hopping Grant, Sandom Lab, University of Sussex
description: A deliberate discipline-hop outside social/affective robotics, applying complex systems and agent-based modelling methods to rewilding and nature-recovery in the UK, in collaboration with ecologist Christopher Sandom. The project explored how participatory modelling can help balance the needs of people and nature-recovery.

outputs.title: A Participatory Complex Systems Modelling Approach Towards Rewilding in the UK

audience: Students and academics interested in interdisciplinary applications of ALife and complex-systems methods beyond HRI or cognitive science.
